business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Catalog Retail of Industrial Maintenance Hardware

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1986, as amended), Title II Article IV investment and nondiscrimination provisions
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus (signed 2017, entered into force 2020)
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA) (entered into force 2006)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Code, Title 51, Business Corporations Act (1990), as amended; Title 52, Registered Agents Act (1990), as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2012 (RMI Public Law No. 2012-75), as amended; Financial Institutions Act 1993, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid national passport (or government-issued photo ID) for each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or national civil registry of the country of nationality or residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the RMI Licensed Registered Agent as local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the applicant's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the RMI Domestic Designated Sanctions List using a licensed automated screening tool. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for Politically Exposed Persons, their immediate family members, and close associates. Periodic rescreening is required at each transaction trigger and at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry Online Filing Portal (administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations; submissions are made through licensed Registered Agents under RMI Code Tit. 51 § 5)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or transliterated into the standard Latin alphabet (A-Z, 0-9, and limited punctuation such as ampersand and hyphen). Marshallese language names must be romanized. Diacritical marks are not accepted in the registered corporate name. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not be misleading or imply governmental connection or a regulated activity without authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 days of notice, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, formal consents from the competent regulatory authority for sensitive words, or a proposed amended name. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, a formal administrative appeal may be submitted to the Minister for Commerce and Tourism within 30 days of the refusal. Final recourse is judicial review in the High Court of the Marshall Islands filed within 30 days of the ministerial determination. A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30-day period by written request before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted and standard for a non-resident B2B e-commerce entity. The registered office must be a physical street address in the Marshall Islands where a licensed registered agent is situated and service of process may be accepted. A P.O. Box alone is insufficient. No local place of business, employees, or operator presence in the Marshall Islands is required for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at less than 5% annualized probability for a non-regulated, low-risk B2B MRO e-commerce business classified under ISIC 4791. However, the supervising licensed registered agent is subject to unannounced on-site inspections by the Registrar of Corporations on a risk-based schedule under the Registered Agents Act and AML/CFT regulations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee schedule under RMI Code Tit. 51; no stamp duty on authorized capital at this tier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Registered Agent appointment and registered office lease (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-resident business corporation registered agent services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO due diligence file preparation (identity verification, PEP and sanctions screening, risk assessment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Customer Due Diligence and UBO piercing under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Third-party reimbursement at prevailing official and notarial tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate kit production, certification extraction, and courier disbursement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations / external counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff or prevailing administrative appeal filing fee, if required

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of 1990 (as codified at 27 MIRC Ch. 1), particularly Sections 17 (Articles of Incorporation), 19 (Registered Office and Agent), 35 (First Board of Directors), and 50 (Corporate Seal).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (online portal: www.mhcorporations.com / e-filing through authorized agents).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1), accompanied by written consent of the registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed. The authorized capital is fixed by the Articles of Incorporation; no escrow or pre-deposit is required. Consideration for subscribed shares must be lawful and need not be paid in full at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation approves the subscription of its authorized shares by the initial shareholder in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation shall be maintained at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and the registered agent is appointed; RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until their successors are duly elected; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the board adopts the corporate seal and authorizes an initial bank mandate with dual signature authority for the President and Secretary; AND FURTHER RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to execute all documents necessary to open bank accounts, complete regulatory filings, and secure any applicable tax exemption certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General (online name reservation queue).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name and one alternate name via the authorized filing portal or direct e-mail to the Registry. The name must include the word 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or the abbreviation 'Inc.' or 'Corp.' to denote limited liability. Pay the name reservation fee electronically and obtain the reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of beneficial owner passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as unavailable or deceptively similar, an amended application with an alternate name may be resubmitted within 5 business days without payment of an additional name search fee; or appeal to the Registrar for an administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public authorized in the Republic of the Marshall Islands or a notary in the jurisdiction where the incorporator signs (with legalization/apostille).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation, including corporate name, purpose, authorized share structure, registered agent name and address, and names of initial directors. Have each incorporator sign in the presence of a notary; the registered agent must sign a separate consent form. Verify that no local address appears in the substantive purpose clause if the corporation will be non-resident.
required_dossiers: Registered Agent Consent / Acceptance of Appointment Form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarization is defective or the document is missing the registered agent signature, the registry will raise a technical correction notice; the applicant must re-execute the Articles with proper notarial certification and resubmit within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations (accepted through authorized registered agent or the online portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation together with the name reservation certificate, registered agent consent, and initial director signatures. Pay the official filing fee of USD 275 via wire transfer or card, whichever is accepted by the Registry. Upon acceptance, the Registry stamps the document and proceeds with processing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate or application number
Payment receipt of official filing fee
Covering letter from the authorized filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency letter, the applicant shall file an amended schedule within 14 calendar days; if the deficiency relates to fees, pay the outstanding amount plus any late surcharge. Submission of a complete response resets the processing clock to 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the statutory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the assigned corporate identification number and seals the Articles. Order a corporate seal and blank share certificates from the authorized service provider, ensuring the name and year of incorporation match the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error, deliver the original certificate and a notarized request for correction within 20 business days; the Registrar will issue a certificate of correction with retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and financial institution (not government-controlled); if tax exemption is requested, the Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. Open a corporate bank account in a selected licensed financial institution overseas or in Majuro, presenting the certificate of incorporation and board resolution. If a tax exemption certificate is desired for non-resident status, file a Form MP-TX1 with the Revenue and Taxation Division.
required_dossiers: Officer and beneficial owner identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further corporate records, provide a certificate of good standing and complete annual report filings; if the tax exemption is challenged, appeal in writing to the Secretary of Finance within 30 days and provide evidence that all income is derived from sources outside the Republic.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable (the registered activity is electronic catalog retail of industrial MRO hardware, ISIC 4791 — no manufacturing, processing, or industrial plant is operated).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for a non-physical, electronic retail and distribution activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is not required for e-commerce retail and warehousing; only a general EPA registration is needed if the warehouse exceeds 1,000 m2 for storage of non-hazardous goods.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Neutral obligations: no process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated. If a warehouse is maintained, comply with the Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Act, 1987: solid waste shall be removed via licensed hauler; stormwater outflows must not cause visible sheen or exceed secondary treatment standards; prohibited use of underground storage tanks for fuel. Retail packaging must meet EPA waste reduction guidelines.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any leased office or warehouse: obtain a fire safety certification from the local fire authority, comply with National Building Code occupancy load and structural load certifications, and secure a workplace health clearance from the Occupational Safety and Health Inspectorate of the Ministry of Health and Human Services; such clearances are not a precondition to incorporation but are required before physical occupation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Revenue and Taxation Division (Majuro). Corporate registration infrastructure: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, operating through licensed RMI Registered Agents; customs administration: RMI Customs Service using the ASYCUDA electronic single-window platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: No statutory TIN or VAT ID is issued to a non-resident Business Corporation (BC) because the RMI does not tax non-resident domestic corporations. Procedure: (1) appoint a licensed RMI Registered Agent and registered office address; (2) file Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (BCCA) designating non-resident domestic corporation status; (3) pay the government filing fee; (4) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of Corporations. The registry number and Certificate of Good Standing serve as the de facto tax identifiers. A Foreign Investment Business License and RMI tax registration become necessary only if the entity commences business activity with RMI-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — Non-Resident Domestic Corporation: a BC designated as non-resident in its articles is statutorily exempt from RMI income tax on all income derived outside the Republic, and is not subject to VAT/GST, capital gains tax, or import duty on outbound supplies, provided it has no RMI-source income and does not carry on business in the RMI; only annual registry/government fee obligations apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None analogous to US check-the-box; RMI has no corporate income tax for non-resident BCs and no hybrid-mismatch rules. Available status elections under the BCCA: (i) resident vs. non-resident domestic corporation designation in the articles; (ii) continuation into/out of the RMI (re-domestication); (iii) conversion between BC, LLC, and partnership forms; (iv) issuance of Certificate of Good Standing. Improper designation or RMI-source activity forfeits the exemption and triggers standard RMI taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax in force. Sole indirect fiscal regime: import duty under the Customs Tariff Act 1990; exports are duty-free. Electronic B2B MRO supplies (ISIC 4791) invoiced abroad attract no RMI indirect tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. RMI official currency is the US dollar (USD); an economic turnover threshold of USD 0 is deemed inapplicable because no indirect tax is imposed on outbound supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API-stamping, or digital control mandate. Where goods physically enter or leave RMI customs territory, declarations are filed electronically through ASYCUDA; ordinary commercial invoices, packing lists, and transport documents are accepted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — absence of a VAT/GST system means no 0% export VAT rate and no VAT refund mechanism. Goods exported from the RMI are free of export duty; industrial MRO inputs imported into the RMI and subsequently re-exported may qualify for customs duty drawback or duty suspension upon documentary proof of import, storage, and export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the ASYCUDA platform (required only when goods physically depart RMI customs territory)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing outbound shipment
Commercial invoice and packing list (inward remittance certificate not required — RMI imposes no exchange controls and uses the US dollar)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No statutory FX repatriation deadline and no VAT zero-rating clawback can arise in the RMI. However, false declarations, drawback fraud, smuggling, or evasion of customs duty under the Customs Tariff Act 1990 subject the exporter to forfeiture, fines, and criminal liability, with the Registrar able to strike off an offending BC for non-compliance; resumption of RMI-source activity without proper FIBL and tax registration exposes the entity to income tax, penalties, and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) has no statutory central bank; the Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance exercises all banking licensing, prudential supervision and foreign-exchange monitoring powers, while the U.S. Federal Reserve System serves as the de facto monetary anchor through the Compact of Free Association. The U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender under RMI law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMI operates a fully dollarized economy with zero exchange-control restrictions. Current-account transactions (trade settlement, shipping and logistics for MRO goods) and capital-account transactions (equity injection, shareholder loans and dividend repatriation) are freely convertible and require no central bank approval. Profit remittance from a non-resident Business Corporation is unrestricted once beneficial-ownership filings are current, the account passes AML/KYC screening, and no unpaid RMI income-tax liability exists for any economic activity conducted within RMI territory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: RMI imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. All MRO electronic-catalog proceeds may be credited and retained indefinitely in USD demand or time deposits held at an RMI-licensed bank, with unrestricted availability for operational disbursements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Capital Escrow Account and USD Operational Treasury Account
USD Operational Account and Trade Finance Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. The RMI Banking Act confines deposit-taking to domestically licensed banks and no RMI electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence exists; therefore a U.S., U.K. or EU-licensed EMI may be used solely as a secondary collection rail for card-not-present MRO payments, with legal settlement forced to an RMI-licensed bank account. Foreign EMIs cannot provide the principal account, cash escrow, or trade-finance clearing structure required by the blueprint.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance by at least one authorized director is the standard mandate: RMI banks require a face-to-face signatory interview, normally in Majuro or Ebeye, to open corporate USD accounts for non-resident Business Corporations. Remote video-KYC is available only on a bank-by-bank exception basis and requires enhanced due diligence, English-language notarization of all corporate documents, and a pre-approved compliance memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and beneficial-ownership transparency red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Business Corporation Charter; Certificate of Good Standing from the RMI Corporate Registry; Registered Agent appointment certificate; signed and notarized Beneficial Ownership Declaration with corporate-structure chart; board resolution designating account signatories; director passports and address proof; equity subscription agreements; and a written Explanatory Memorandum mapping the ISIC 4791 electronic-catalog B2B MRO model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: U.S. OFAC, adverse-media and politically-exposed-person screening hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-match OFAC and UN sanctions-screening certificates; reputable AML-database and adverse-media due-diligence report; PEP declaration with source-of-wealth attestation from each ultimate beneficial owner; government-issued identity documentation; and reference letters from retained international counsel and the Registered Agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared e-commerce scope and projected wire/FX flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: B2B marketplace and supplier contracts; ISIC-4791 order and ERP records; warehouse or fulfillment-center leases; freight-forwarder bills of lading; card-acquirer platform underwriting; and a 12-month projected cash-flow model containing clearly labelled payment references for each expected inbound and outbound wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk card-not-present and cross-border card-acquiring activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS compliant attestation of the merchant processor; documented chargeback and refund governance policy; B2B minimum-order and credit-terms policy; 3-D Secure authentication adoption; fraud-prevention controls; and the merchant agreement proving legitimate operation of the electronic industrial MRO catalog.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial shareholder equity or shareholder-loan capital is wired via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder home-country bank to the RMI-licensed USD account using ISO 20022 narrative EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / OPERATIONAL TREASURY INJECTION and crediting instructions read by the U.S. correspondent bank for OFAC screening. The compliant packet comprises the notarized board resolution, share subscription agreement, source-of-funds statement, Certificate of Good Standing and beneficial-ownership schedule. Correspondent clearing should route through JPMorgan, Citibank, Bank of America or Wells Fargo to minimize U.S. intermediary friction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor settlement and MT202 for inter-company treasury concentration. High-value MRO procurement from Asia-Pacific suppliers is executed through Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600, with MT707 amendment messaging, and USD disbursements settle across CHIPS and Fedwire via the U.S. correspondent network. Payment narratives must mirror purchase-order reference numbers to survive bank compliance review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD forward contracts on cross-currency invoice flows with investment-grade U.S. or European bank counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) against non-convertible emerging-market currencies (onshore CNY, INR, IDR, VND)
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for structural exposure hedging
European-style vanilla foreign-exchange options for defined risk-limits
LME-linked commodity hedging forwards for MRO steel, copper and aluminum input costs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report (Annual Confirmation of Directors, Officers, Shareholders, and Beneficial Owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance and Banking
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of incorporation; filing accepted within 30 days following the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty plus US$100 delinquency surcharge; continued failure may lead to suspension of corporate standing and administrative strike-off after 90 days from the anniversary date

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit for a non-resident Business Corporation; a mandatory audit is triggered only if the corporation conducts business within the Marshall Islands, holds a licensed/regulated activity, or if shareholders holding 10% or more of voting shares request an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) accepted; no local GAAP and no statutory requirement to file financial statements with the Registry

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Annual Corporate Report must confirm current beneficial ownership and ownership percentage; any change in shareholders or beneficial owners must be recorded in the register of beneficial owners and filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the underlying transfer.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a non-resident Business Corporation with tax-exempt status; no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, and no payroll tax are imposed by the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) on income derived from sources outside the RMI. A 3% Gross Revenue Tax applies solely to gross revenue derived from trade or business carried on within the Marshall Islands; offshore catalog sales of industrial MRO supplies fall outside the charge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income-tax exemption for Non-Resident Domestic Corporations under the Business Corporations Act and related tax-exemption rulings. Additional incentives: nil income-tax return filing; no dividend, interest, or royalty withholding; no alternative minimum tax; no controlled-foreign-company regime; no estate, gift, or net-worth taxes. The 3% Gross Revenue Tax is charged at zero on non-resident entities without physical presence, permanent establishment, or local procurement activity in the RMI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Business Corporation Annual Report (prescribed form under the Business Corporations Act, Title 50 RMI Code) filed exclusively through the official corporate registry e-filing portal of the Registrar of Corporations. The annual license fee is paid in the same submission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the 30th day of the calendar month following the anniversary date of incorporation. A late-filed report attracts penalties, and continued non-filing for two consecutive years subjects the corporation to administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name, corporate registration number, date of incorporation, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the name exactly as shown on the Articles of Incorporation; use the actual fiscal year end (e.g., December 31) consistent with audited records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and Majuro office address of the licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a current RMI-licensed agent maintaining a physical office in Majuro; the offshore beneficial owner cannot act as its own registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Street address of the principal office, which may be outside the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the operational head-office address (e.g., Singapore or regional hub); a P.O. box alone is insufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationalities, and residential addresses of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each director individually; nominee directors must be identified as such. The BCA requires at least one director, and directors need not be RMI residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total authorized and issued shares, classes of shares, par value, and details of any convertible instruments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State issued share count and consideration; non-resident ownership is unrestricted and minimum capital is not required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of non-resident tax-exempt status and confirmation that no trade or business was conducted within the Marshall Islands during the reporting year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the non-resident tax-exempt box only if no local-source activities exist; false declarations trigger criminal penalties and loss of exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the statutory annual license fee based on issued share count or fixed base amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Rates are tiered under the BCA fee schedule; pay via wire or through the registered agent with proof of payment retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of approximately USD 50 per month, capped at USD 300 per report; failure to file for two consecutive years results in automatic administrative dissolution. Reinstatement requires payment of all outstanding fees and penalties plus a reinstatement application fee, and a Certificate of Good Standing must be obtained before any contract, bank account, or legal proceeding is recognized.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Gross Revenue Tax Return (Form GRT-1) and Business License Renewal, filed with the Ministry of Finance, Treasury and Accounting (Revenue Division) for any entity engaging in trade or business within the Marshall Islands.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly estimated installments where the prior-year gross revenue tax liability exceeded USD 2,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due on or before April 30 following the close of the tax year; quarterly installments due by the 10th day of the month following each calendar quarter. Non-resident zero-filers must still submit the annual return to preserve eligibility for the business license exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from sources within the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including imports, local sales, and services performed in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero for offshore B2B MRO catalog sales where order acceptance, invoicing, payment, and delivery occur outside the RMI and no local agent or warehouse exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory exemptions, including gross revenue of approved non-resident corporations and revenue from exports or transshipments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the non-resident tax-exempt deduction supported by the annual report tax-status declaration and board resolutions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue after exemptions, being the base for the 3% tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Should normally be zero; any positive amount must be reconciled with local contracts, customs entries, and bank statements.
Self-assessed and payable in USD; no credit is available against foreign income taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of business license status, place of business, and employee headcount within the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare no local place of business, no local employees, and no local warehouse; attach a short board statement if requested.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of the tax due; monthly interest of 1% on arrears; non-filing results in business license suspension and, for taxpayers with local assets, distress seizure and public auction. For non-resident zero-filers, repeated non-filing triggers loss of tax-exempt certificate status and intensified scrutiny by the Revenue Division.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the Marshall Islands imposes no withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Business Corporation to non-resident shareholders, regardless of share class or amount.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI maintains no comprehensive double-taxation agreements. Consequently, treaty relief is not available; a shareholder claiming a foreign tax credit in its residence jurisdiction must rely on the RMI Certificate of Tax Existence issued by the Ministry of Finance upon submission of: (1) the annual report filing receipt; (2) a certified copy of the tax-status declaration; (3) a registered-agent certificate; and (4) a board resolution declaring the dividend. The certificate is discretionary, non-statutory, and issued only for corporations in good standing. It does not alter the 0% statutory rate and cannot create treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding on IP royalties and debt interest paid to non-residents; no treaty rates apply because no income tax conventions are in force. Payments may flow freely; however, the payer must retain arm's-length documentation (licensing agreements, loan notes, interest-rate benchmarks) to support deductions or foreign tax credit claims before foreign tax authorities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No domestic transfer-pricing legislation or Local File / Master File regime exists in the RMI. As a compliance benchmark, mandatory documentation would only be contemplated where local-source gross revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 (gross revenue tax threshold) and related-party transactions affect the RMI tax base; for a tax-exempt non-resident BC with no RMI permanent establishment, the effective documentation threshold is nil and no transfer-pricing return is filed.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations comparable to BVI or Cayman, but it participates in OECD/G20 inclusive framework transparency reviews and maintains a FATF-consistent AML regime. A non-resident BC operating a B2B MRO catalog must demonstrate real economic substance — independent board meetings, actual procurement and distribution functions, a funded bank account, and retention of commercial risk — to prevent recharacterization of the RMI entity as a sham in the shareholder's jurisdiction and to preserve access to foreign tax credits under CFC, PFIC, and GAAR rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely declaring non-resident tax-exempt status in the annual report while conducting trade within the Marshall Islands; understating local-source gross revenue on the GRT-1 return; destroying invoices or shipping records to conceal revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Gross Revenue Tax Act and the Business Corporations Act: 20% penalty on tax underpaid plus interest of 1% per month; criminal fines of USD 5,000 to USD 25,000 per false filing; revocation of tax-exempt status; retroactive assessment for three years; administrative dissolution of the corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each signing director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and restitution; conviction carries imprisonment of up to 5 years; the court may issue travel bans and asset-freeze orders; the corporate veil is pierced upon proof that the declaration was made with knowledge of falsity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC as a bare invoice pass-through in the industrial MRO supply chain — no bank account, no staff, no board meetings, no procurement risk — while related parties in other jurisdictions perform all functions and retain all profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI does not levy a domestic penalty for lack of substance, but adverse OECD/FATF peer-review results and EU listing produce defensive withholding and de-risking: correspondent banks close accounts, and foreign tax authorities recharacterize the structure, imposing 30% penalties and interest on the economic owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors knowingly facilitating the sham are exposed to civil claims for damages in RMI courts; managing directors can be disqualified from acting as directors for up to 10 years; foreign criminal courts may issue arrest warrants, making travel outside the RMI high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving SWIFT wire payments from unidentified B2B buyers without customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit, or structuring credit-card receipts at sub-threshold amounts to avoid record-keeping obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Entity fines of up to USD 100,000 per violation; failure to file a suspicious transaction report attracts an additional USD 50,000 fine; continued non-compliance compels the registered agent to withdraw representation and the Registrar to strike the corporation from the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Willful blindness is treated as aiding and abetting: directors face imprisonment of up to 10 years, personal confiscation orders, disqualification orders, and travel bans pending extradition; the corporate veil is pierced for fraud, and directors bear joint liability for laundered amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC to conceal economic ownership from foreign tax authorities, failing to comply with FATCA reporting obligations under the RMI-United States intergovernmental agreement, or wiring MRO proceeds to personal accounts of U.S. or EU tax residents without full recordkeeping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FATCA 30% withholding on U.S.-source payments; RMI financial institutions breach compliance obligations and may be fined; listing in the EU non-cooperative jurisdiction annex triggers 25% defensive withholding on EU payments to RMI entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly assist foreign tax evasion face extradition and criminal liability in the residence state, asset-freezing orders, and confiscation of personal assets; the absence of RMI domestic income tax does not shield a director from foreign civil fraud claims.
